data.title: SDMC's Third Consecutive Year at Google's TV Summit, Showcasing Home Physical AI
data.description:
BANGKOK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At Google's 2026 TV Summit in Bangkok, SDMC (00901.HK) returned as an invited speaker for the third consecutive year, advancing its AI Home strategy under the theme "Building the Future of Home Physical AI with Google".

Building on Google's ecosystem and technologies, SDMC introduced an innovative product concept. We further advanced Edge AI innovation with Amlogic, delivered a joint presentation with Altice Labs on TV Centric Home Physical AI, and signed an MOU to establish an AI Home Joint Innovation Lab.

From Connected Homes to Home Physical AI

At this year's TV Summit, SDMC explored Home Physical AI—intelligence that senses household conditions, understands context, and acts in the physical environment.

We envision the TV and living room as the center of the Home AI Agent experience—a shared screen in a shared space where family members can interact with AI together.

To explore this vision and inspire next-generation home experiences, we showcased the Cedar Display Hub, a concept prototype that combines an Android TV streaming dock with a companion second screen. Demonstrations included AI recaps without interrupting playback, cross-screen family games, home-camera highlights on TV, and more.

Connecting Google and Edge AI Technologies

Android TV and Google TV underpin entertainment, while Cedar combines Gemma-based Edge AI with Gemini-powered cloud reasoning for context-aware assistance. SDMC integrates these capabilities across devices and software and participates in Google Cloud's Proactive Physical AI Acceleration Program.

With Amlogic, SDMC demonstrated Edge AI for personalized interaction and family memory management. The A311Y3-powered Display Hub uses voiceprint and facial recognition to distinguish family members; the S905D5-powered AI NAS Frame supports recognition, classification, and search of locally stored family photos.

Building AI Home Services for Operators

For operators, SDMC's AI Home portfolio builds on established TV and broadband services. Its AI Streaming Box brings AI-enhanced entertainment, whole-home control, and family security to the TV; Google TV Projector extends premium viewing; and AI Fiber Gateway provides Wi-Fi 8 and XGS-PON connectivity.

AI Operation adds proactive monitoring, unified device management, and closed-loop support, helping operators explore new service opportunities and deepen household engagement.

Advancing Joint Innovation & Commercial Validation

These opportunities were also central to SDMC's joint presentation with Altice Labs. SDMC explained how Home AI Agents complement personal assistants and how cloud-edge AI enables dual-screen family experiences. Altice Labs drew on Sophia, its upcoming MEO TV assistant, to discuss the shift from on-demand responses toward proactive assistance.

Under the MOU, SDMC and Altice Labs plan to establish the AI Home Joint Innovation Lab, combining SDMC's integration capabilities with Altice Labs' operator expertise to explore family assistance, home security, and whole-home control. Selected scenarios are planned for a field pilot in Portugal, with commercial validation targeted for 2027.

Together, these efforts aim to make Home Physical AI useful for families and viable for operators.

data.description: Saputo's C$600 million capacity expansion into high-growth, value-added dairy categories should be a longer-term benefit for its shares, according to CIBC in a note. Analyst Tal Woolley says the investment will focus on cottage cheese, functional/high-protein beverages and cream cheese, "where demand remains strong and existing capacity is constrained." data.title: Wall Street trades lower as the tech space remains under heavy pressure
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages were mixed on Friday, as a further tech selloff has put the main indices on track for their steepest weekly declines in over a year, as fresh weakness in artificial intelligence stocks fueled wider market concerns.

The blue-chip Dow was last +0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite was last -1.6%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, eight of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with consumer staples leading the way higher, while info tech has been the weakest area.

Sentiment toward artificial intelligence stocks remained under pressure after Anthropic's much-anticipated public market debut failed to provide the boost investors had hoped for, extending a volatile week for equities.

The latest declines followed a bruising Thursday session in which all three major indexes fell more than 2%, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield dropped 9 basis points to 4.67%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield shifted down 8 basis points to 4.96%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield moved down 5 basis points to 5.35%.

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Fair Isaac Corp. advanced +6.2%, while shares of Sandisk dropped -10.5%.

data.title: CNH Names Paul Dick, President, North America
data.description:
Key points:
  • Paul Dick appointed President, North America, effective Jan. 1, 2027
  • Scott Harris to retire from role after 20 years with CNH and serve as senior advisor in 2027

Paul Dick, President of North America CNH

Basildon, UK — November 20, 2026 — CNH Industrial N.V. today announced the appointment of Paul Dick as president, North America, effective Jan. 1, 2027. Dick will succeed Scott Harris, who is retiring next year after 20 distinguished years with the company.

Harris will serve as president, North America, through Dec. 31. Beginning Jan. 1, Dick will assume the role, and Harris will remain with CNH as a senior advisor in 2027 to support a smooth transition.

"Scott Harris has given CNH 20 remarkable years, and the North America business he leaves behind is stronger, more connected to our dealers and better positioned for the future because of him," said Gerrit Marx, Chief Executive Officer of CNH. "He has shaped our dealer network, mentored countless leaders and set a standard of integrity and customer focus that defines who we are in North America. On behalf of the entire CNH team, I thank Scott for his countless contributions and wish him every happiness in this next chapter. We are fortunate that Scott will stay on to ensure Paul and the team are set up for continued success."

"Paul Dick is the right leader for the next chapter of North America. He brings a rare combination of operational discipline, services and recurring revenue expertise, and an authentic, lifelong connection to the agricultural equipment our customers depend on. His track record of driving margin expansion while scaling digital and connected solutions aligns directly with our strategic priorities and our Path to 2030," Marx said.

"It has been the honor of my career to lead this team," Harris said. "The dealers, employees and customers who make up CNH's North America business are the best in the industry. I'm proud of what we've built together, and I will leave with complete confidence in Paul and in the future of this business."

Dick is a senior operating executive with more than two decades of leadership experience in complex industrial businesses. In his most recent role at Ingersoll Rand, he led a team responsible for sales to key accounts directly and through a wide distribution, direct and retail network spanning from consumer products to large professional systems. He has led major business integrations and digital transformation initiatives.

“I’ve had a lifelong connection to agriculture and a deep respect for the people who depend on this industry every day. That makes the opportunity to lead CNH North America especially meaningful to me,” Dick said. “I look forward to working with our teams and dealers to build on the strong foundation already in place, move quickly on opportunities for growth and deliver exceptional outcomes for our customers and our business.”

Dick holds a master’s degree in industrial management and a bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering technology from the University of Central Missouri.

***

About CNH

CNH serves and advances the people who feed and build a growing world.

We are an iron-and-tech company, engineering intelligence, automation, and precision into the machines that move the global economy. Our equipment operates in more than 160 geographies, supported by a global team of more than 34,000 people, including engineers, technologists, and industry experts.

Our brands — Case IH, New Holland, STEYR, CNH Tech (including the Raven precision technology platform), and CNH Capital — together generated $18.1B in revenue in 2025.

Building on a legacy of innovation dating back to 1842, CNH has achieved multiple milestones including the first mass-produced tractor, the first twin-rotor combine, and the first factory-integrated precision farming system. Today, we are engineering autonomous and predictive machines that will shape the future of food and infrastructure.

data.title: Bulls on a roll. Nifty hit 9-month high as Rupee logs best weekly rally in 5 weeks; Bond yields ease
data.description:
Indian markets capped another strong week on Friday, extending their winning streak to four consecutive weeks and pushing benchmark indices to their highest levels in nine months as robust foreign inflows powered gains across equities, bonds and the currency market.

The Nifty 50 closed at a nine-month high of 25,800.60, while the Sensex ended at 83,919.71, marking the benchmarks’ fourth consecutive week of gains. Banking stocks remained the market’s biggest driver, with the Bank Nifty hitting a fresh record high of 64,680.80 before settling at 64,635, up 2.49 per cent for the day and nearly 16 per cent so far this month.

“The banking sector was leading from the front this week and closed with a whopping weekly gain of 5.9 per cent,” said Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities.

Foreign portfolio investors continued to dominate flows, pumping over ₹1 lakh crore into Indian equities during November so far, helping markets shrug off concerns around global technology stocks and elevated US yields. Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said improving earnings visibility and a strengthening rupee have reinforced India’s appeal among overseas investors.

Rupee roars

The rupee emerged as the week’s standout performer, posting its strongest weekly gain in five weeks. The currency appreciated 1.67 per cent, or 157 paise, against the US dollar during the week, closing at 92.67 compared with 94.24 levels seen at the start of the week. On Friday alone, it gained 62 paise from the previous close of 93.29, climbing to its strongest level in about seven months despite the Dollar Index hovering near a 20-month high.

“Sustained FII inflows and positive domestic market sentiment could keep the rupee on a firm trajectory,” said Jateen Trivedi, Vice President, Research Analyst at LKP Securities.

Kunal Sodhani, Head-Treasury at Shinhan Bank, said the rupee’s resilience reflected a combination of strong foreign inflows, softer crude oil prices and a reversal in global investment flows towards emerging markets. “To prevent excessive rupee appreciation, the RBI may intervene through dollar purchases or encourage oil marketing companies to source part of their dollar requirements from the open market,” he added.

Crude cools

Falling crude oil prices also strengthened sentiment across asset classes. Brent crude eased to around $90 a barrel during the week, improving India’s macroeconomic outlook by lowering concerns around imported inflation and the current account deficit.

The bond market also joined the rally. Government security yields softened as declining crude oil prices and easing US Treasury yields improved sentiment. The benchmark 6.94 per cent GS 2036 yield fell 6 basis points during the session to close at 7.19 per cent from 7.25 per cent previously, signalling continued demand for sovereign debt.

Lower oil prices, resilient domestic growth prospects and sustained foreign inflows have created a favourable backdrop for Indian assets, said experts. With equities at nine-month highs, the rupee at a seven-month peak and bond yields easing, investors will closely track upcoming US inflation data and month-end derivatives expiry for further cues on the direction of foreign flows.

data.title: Nigeria rescue teams search for survivors after funeral barge capsizes in Bayelsa
data.description:
By Tife Owolabi

Rescue workers are searching for survivors after a crowded barge carrying people to a funeral capsized in Nigeria's southern Bayelsa state, with several passengers feared dead, police and local residents said on Friday.

  • The vessel capsized on waterways near Ukubie in Bayelsa state's Southern Ijaw area while carrying passengers to a funeral, according to residents

  • Bayelsa police spokesperson Musa Mohammed said a marine unit has been deployed to assist rescue operations

  • The police did not immediately provide the number of people killed, rescued or missing

  • Sophie Igoniwari, a witness, said chaotic boarding and overcrowding preceded the boat's departure from Anyama Ijaw, and that several victims were brought ashore after it capsized shortly afterwards

  • Boat accidents are common on Nigeria's inland waterways, especially in riverine communities where overcrowding is widespread and safety regulations are often flouted

data.title: New Insperity Research Highlights the Importance of HR Support for Small Businesses
data.description:
Insperity, Inc. (), a leading provider of human resources and business performance solutions, released "Reclaim Your Leadership with Expert HR Support," new research conducted in partnership with Lighthouse Research & Advisory, which found that managing HR administration internally consumes leaders’ time and diverts attention from business growth.

According to the study, nearly half (46%) of leaders surveyed at businesses with fewer than 150 employees say HR administration distracts them from moving the business forward, 45% say it limits their ability to think strategically and more than one-third (37%) have delayed growth or expansion planning because of HR administrative demands.

“As a company grows, so does the volume and complexity of managing its people and the rapidly evolving AI era is adding new considerations,” said Steve Arizpe, president and chief operating officer of Insperity. “Having the right HR support helps business leaders navigate that complexity with confidence, so they can stay focused on taking care of their people and moving their company forward.”

The right HR support can reclaim leadership capacity for business growth

As HR demands become more complex, many leaders are looking to outside HR support to create more administrative efficiency, improve employee experience, align teams with business goals and provide proactive compliance guidance.

Among the surveyed leaders of companies with fewer than 150 employees using outside HR support, 94% saw a difference bringing on external HR experts with 60% saying they have been able to redirect time towards business growth and revenue, 49% stating they could spend more time on strategic planning and 47% claiming they put more time into strengthening customer relationships.

These findings highlight the importance of investing in HR as a strategic business function, giving leaders more time and energy for strategy, growth and their people.

To learn more about the research and download the report, “Reclaim Your Leadership with Expert HR Support,” click here.

About the Study

The findings in Reclaim Your Leadership with Expert HR Support come from the 2026 Hidden Cost of HR Administration Study, conducted by Lighthouse Research & Advisory in partnership with Insperity. The full study surveyed 832 U.S. business leaders in 2026. The report focuses on 418 respondents at organizations with fewer than 150 employees. Nearly all respondents held senior leadership roles: 84% were owners or founders and another 14% were CEOs, presidents, managing partners or other senior executives. Just 2% were HR leaders or managers.

About Insperity

Since 1986, Insperity’s mission has been to help businesses succeed so communities prosper. Offering a suite of the most comprehensive, scalable HR solutions available in the marketplace, Insperity is defined by an unrivaled breadth and depth of services and level of care. Through an optimal blend of premium HR service and technology, Insperity delivers the administrative relief, reduced liabilities and better benefit solutions that businesses need to drive performance and growth. With 2025 revenues of $6.8 billion and sales and service operations throughout the U.S., Insperity is currently making a difference in thousands of businesses and communities nationwide. For more information, visit http://www.insperity.com.

data.title: First Solar CEO Urges Bipartisan Support for Industrial Strategy, Enforcement of US Trade and Tax Policy at House Select Committee on China Hearing
data.description:
Mark Widmar, chief executive officer of First Solar, Inc. () (“First Solar” or “the Company”), today urged bipartisan support for an industrial strategy and the enforcement of American trade and tax laws to sustain domestic manufacturing growth.

At the invitation of Chairman John Moolenaar (R-Mich.), Widmar testified before the United States House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (the House Select Committee on China).

Addressing the committee at the hearing on “Outproducing the CCP: Restoring American Manufacturing,” Widmar said, “American technology, American factories, American workers, and consistent enforcement of our trade and tax laws are not Democratic priorities or Republican ones. They are American ones.”

First Solar is the country’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company and the only one of the world’s largest solar manufacturers to be headquartered in the US. The Company operates six manufacturing facilities in Alabama, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina; R&D centers in Ohio and California; and a solar technology testing center in Arizona. By the end of 2026, First Solar expects to have invested over $5 billion in American manufacturing and R&D infrastructure since 2019, and by 2027 it forecasts approximately 17 GW of US nameplate module manufacturing capacity.

“First Solar is here as proof that America can rebuild manufacturing capacity,” Widmar said. “We didn’t invest approximately $5 billion in American manufacturing because it was easy. We invested because we believe in the American worker.”

Citing tax and trade policies across multiple administrations that catalyzed domestic solar manufacturing growth, Widmar noted, “The lesson is that industrial strategy must be bipartisan. When the rules hold from one Administration and Congress to the next, entire markets can grow, and domestic manufacturers can invest with certainty in the United States.”

Widmar noted the range of trade remedies available to help level the playing field for American workers and manufacturers and cited the Section 232 action on polysilicon as an example of a targeted remedy — one aimed at a specific national security risk or economic abuse and applied where there is domestic capacity to build. He said, “On behalf of all of our American workers, I thank President Trump and Secretary Lutnick for the first true acknowledgment that the solar supply chain is a national security issue.”

The full hearing is available on demand here.

About First Solar, Inc.

First Solar, Inc. is America’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company. The only US-headquartered company among the world’s largest solar manufacturers, First Solar is focused on competitively and reliably enabling power generation needs with its advanced, uniquely American thin film PV technology. Developed at R&D labs in California and Ohio, the Company’s technology provides a competitive, high-performance, and responsibly produced alternative to conventional crystalline silicon PV modules. For more information, please visit www.firstsolar.com.

data.title: The 11 Retirement-Planning Milestones Everyone Over 50 Needs to Know — WSJ
Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
data.description:
Key points:
  • ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
  • Judges say genocide can coexist with military aims
  • South Africa says ruling sets important precedent for state genocide

By Anthony Deutsch and Stephanie van den Berg

The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over the war in Gaza, legal experts said, establishing a precedent that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective.

While the conflicts in Gaza and Myanmar are legally distinct, both cases before the World Court are based on allegations that states breached their obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention.

On Thursday, the court found that Myanmar had violated the convention on multiple grounds stemming from mistreatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority by the armed forces.

South Africa, which has brought a genocide case against Israel over its conduct in Gaza, welcomed the judgment. Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola said it set an important precedent by establishing for the first time that a state had committed genocide. He said it was of "great significance" to the case against Israel, which is not expected to be argued until 2029.

Both Myanmar and Israel have defended the actions of their armed forces as legitimate responses to insurgencies. But a majority of nine judges on the 15-member bench found that around 10,000 killings, including of children, the razing of homes, widespread sexual violence and the forced exodus of more than 700,000 people in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.

The ruling also handed other major legal victories to Gambia, which brought the case seven years ago on behalf of Muslim-majority countries.

The judges found that Myanmar had failed in its obligation to prevent genocide and said it must facilitate the return of Rohingya refugees and pay unspecified reparations.

The court also adopted conclusions from UN fact-finding reports, including one stating that mass deaths and rapes showed genocidal intent.

IMPORTANT PRECEDENT

Israeli legal scholar Yuval Shany said the ruling could broaden the arguments available to South Africa in its case against Israel.

He said the court maintained a requirement that genocidal intent be the “only reasonable inference,” but expanded the contextual factors it can consider beyond a pattern of conduct, to include the scale and systematic nature of acts and the history of persecution.

The approach “gives South Africa more avenues to argue for genocide” in Gaza, Shany said.

Proving genocide is notoriously difficult because it requires establishing an "intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such."

Five criminal acts can constitute genocide: killing members of a group, causing them serious bodily or mental harm, creating conditions calculated to destroy them, preventing births, or forcibly transferring children to ​other groups.

Lamola said South Africa would study the judgment carefully with a view to demonstrating, as the court had in the Rohingya case, that a state's actions, including ethnic cleansing, the killing of children, sexual violence and destruction of civilian infrastructure, can fall within the definition of genocide.

TARGETING OF CHILDREN, WOMEN

Another aspect of the ruling that could resonate in the Israel case was the court's emphasis on the systematic nature and scale of the crimes committed in Myanmar, said Marieke de Hoon, professor of international criminal law at the University of Amsterdam.

South Africa alleges that Israel's military operations created conditions intended to prevent births and disproportionately affected women and children in Gaza. In its filing to the ICJ, it said an estimated 70% of those killed were non-combatants. Israel rejects those allegations and says its operations have been conducted in accordance with international law.

"Arguments that a military intent or military objective would erase the idea that there could be a genocide intent are now rejected by the court," said De Hoon.

She said the judges found that some acts, including attacks on children and women and sexual violence, could not be explained by military objectives alone, leaving genocide as the only reasonable inference.

The Hague Initiative for International Cooperation (Thinc), a think tank funded by pro-Israeli groups, said the judgment would fundamentally alter how courts assess allegations of genocide by imposing a "lower threshold for proving genocidal intent, with serious consequences for Western militaries engaged in confronting terror," such as after Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

It is "not only a verdict in a particular case but a template," Thinc's director, Andrew Tucker, wrote in a reaction.

"Its propositions will be used in future cases: that genocidal intent may coexist with legitimate military objectives...that UN reports compiled without access can carry decisive weight; and that a state can breach the duty to prevent genocide without any finding that genocide occurred."

While the World Court judgment unequivocally found Myanmar responsible for genocide, proving the crime in court remains difficult, said Richard Horsey, senior adviser for Asia at the International Crisis Group.

"The ICJ has never before found that a state committed genocide. The legal bar is extremely high, but what this case shows is that it is surmountable,” he said.

data.title: Nvidia Falls Behind Alphabet, Loses $2.3 Trillion In Market Value Since October Peak
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares were on track to post a seven-day losing streak if losses hold till market close on Friday.
  • The company’s market capitalization has dropped about 41% from its early October peak.
  • Nvidia held the top spot among U.S. companies for much of the year before its recent decline in market value.

Nvidia’s (NVDA) market capitalization fell behind Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) in morning trade on Friday, making it the fourth most valuable U.S. company.

NVDA stock was down 4.6% in morning trading, extending a seven-day losing streak and hitting a fresh 16-month low, while GOOGL stock rose around 2.5%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Nvidia trended in ‘extremely bullish’ zone over the past day, while sentiment around Alphabet trended in the ‘bearish’ zone.

Alphabet’s market value was $3.44 trillion at the time of writing, against $3.41 trillion for Nvidia, a gap of about $30 billion.

Nvidia’s market value peaked near $5.7 trillion in early October, and is now about 41% below that level.

Technology Stocks Lead Market Declines

U.S. equities were mixed in morning trade on Friday. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) was down 0.76%, the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) gained 0.36%, while the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) plummeted over 2%. Retail sentiment around QQQ on Stocktwits trended in ‘bullish’ territory over the past day.

The weakness extended across the semiconductor sector. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell 5.7%, with Credo Technology Group (CRDO) and Coherent (COHR) leading losses. CRDO stock and COHR were both down around about 10%.

Micron Technology (MU) declined 9.5%, while Broadcom (AVGO) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) fell more than 7%.

Nvidia’s Strong Results Have Not Stemmed the Slide

Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier and above analyst estimates of $108.7 billion, according to Koyfin. Earnings per share came in at $2.68, compared with estimates of $2.47.

The company projected revenue of $130 billion for the January quarter and raised its growth outlook to 75% from 70%. Despite the strong results and outlook, the stock has continued to decline.

The leadership transition continued to add to the uncertainty surrounding the company. Nvidia disclosed last week that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO, with Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress appointed interim CEO.

Apple Remains The Most Valuable US Company

Apple (AAPL) remained the most valuable U.S. company, with a market capitalization of about $5.08 trillion, according to Koyfin. Microsoft (MSFT) ranked second at $3.73 trillion, followed by Alphabet and Nvidia.

Amazon (AMZN) ranked fifth, with a market value of approximately $2.80 trillion, around $615 billion below Nvidia.

Nvidia held the top spot among U.S. companies for much of the year before its recent decline in market value.
